name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It preserves fine details in complex scenes better than standard upscalers, giving us a measurable quality bump without extra compute cost. The trade-off is longer render times for high-res frames, but the 0.5%+ capability gain justifies it.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscalers won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop because the core problem is motion blur from fast camera movement, not detail loss. RealVisXL 5.0’s face lock won’t fix it either—it locks *style*, not motion. Test both on a 10-frame burst with 30° camera pan; if face fidelity doesn’t improve, the upscaler’s a dead end.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add RealVisXL 5.0’s face lock to EXCAVA’s pipeline now. Faces are the bottleneck—blur from fast motion destroys fidelity, and no upscaler recovers what’s lost. The trade-off is higher compute cost per frame, but locking face clarity alone will lift overall quality by 0.5%+ without touching the rest of the pipeline. Test it on the same 10-frame burst with 30° camera pan; if faces stay sharp, we keep it.

name: Torque
text: RealVisXL 5.0’s face lock won’t fix EXCAVA’s motion blur—it locks *style*, not motion. The real risk is wasting compute on a band-aid while the core problem (fast camera pan) remains unaddressed. Test depth-aware upscaling *plus* a motion-deblur model (e.g., RestoreFormer++ or a custom LoRA trained on blurred faces) on the same 10-frame burst; if face fidelity improves *without* style drift, that’s the path forward.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Combine InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler with a motion-deblur model (RestoreFormer++ or custom LoRA) to attack EXCAVA’s worst-case 10-frame burst with 30° camera pan; the artifact is a side-by-side quality metric report showing ≥0.5% fidelity gain on faces and fine details, owned by Torque.
